features.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
features.desc: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
body: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.
That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings.
Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days — like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

features.headline: In Mexico City, 49ers' Fred Warner can represent his heritage and boost DPOY case
features.desc: Warner will represent his heritage again Sunday in Mexico City. This time while in the middle of the best Defensive Player of the Year campaign of his career.
body: MEXICO CITY — Taken four years ago to the day, the photo still follows San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner just about anywhere he goes.

It was a brisk Mexico City night in 2022 when Warner — clad in his white No. 54 jersey, gold pants and gold helmet — burst out of the tunnel waving the red, white and green Mexican flag that represents a significant part of his heritage.
The Niners were technically the visiting team against the Cardinals. But as the roar of the crowd enveloped him, Warner felt instantly at home.

Since that game, he has come across the image everywhere from autograph lines — where fans hand him copies to sign — to his childhood home, where his mother, Laura, keeps a blown-up print. For a player building a Hall of Fame résumé, that pregame sprint remains a defining memory.
His reaction every time he sees it? Goosebumps.

"I don't think I understood the magnitude of the moment," Warner told ESPN on Thursday, his 30th birthday. "Being in Mexico in front of the fans, really representing them and representing that part of me and my family was bigger than I even thought."
Watching from her home in San Diego in 2022, Laura Warner saw her son's arrival with the flag in hand as the ultimate public tribute to the roots her late father passed down to their family.
"I just got chills because it was just, to me, a big moment," Laura Warner said. "Because he was representing that heritage of our family in front of everyone."

19, 1996, in San Marcos, California, the ninth-year linebacker leads the 49ers back to Mexico City for a Sunday night showdown against the Minnesota Vikings (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC) in a game with major implications for the NFC's No. 1 seed.

features.headline: How Steelers' wide receiver corps gets big boost in Week 11
features.desc: DK Metcalf and the passing game are poised to get a lift this week with the return of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr.
body: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has never had a season like this.
A career-worst 7% drop rate. Catching a career-low 49.3% of his targets. Averaging, you guessed it, a career-low 48 yards per game and 12.3 yards per reception.

Amid the lows, though, the 28-year-old still made a handful of special plays. There was the 22-yard touchdown reception late in the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and the 32-yard catch-and-run earlier in the game.
There was also the 115-yard game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 and the 11-catch outing in the overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6.

"This is the first time for real," Metcalf said of his struggles Thursday. "But I don't look at it as inconsistency. It's just new territory that I got to maneuver through.... I've just got to block out the bulls—- y'all be talking about, basically."

Metcalf, who was acquired by the historically conservative organization in a blockbuster deal that included a second-round pick on the eve of 2025 free agency, was supposed to be a focal point of the offense.

Instead, the mercurial wide receiver has been defined more by volatility than reliability, and this season, his 49.3% catch rate is second worst in the league out of 133 qualified players, per ESPN Research.
His teammates, though, have remained vocal in their support of him, and the coaching staff has shouldered some of the blame, saying it has to scheme up better opportunities for Metcalf.

"He's been up and down this season, and he's the first to admit that," tight end Pat Freiermuth said. "We need consistency out of him, but I've never worried about if his mind's in the right place or if he's willing to go out there and play.

features.headline: Why Amarius Mims is an underrated key to Bengals' success
features.desc: Joe Burrow is on an MVP trajectory, and a big reason is his OL, led by Amarius Mims.
body: CINCINNATI — One plane ride was all it took for Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Amarius Mims to realize enough was enough.

In last year's Week 4 loss to the Denver Broncos, Mims turned in a performance that made his stomach turn — seven pressures and 1.5 sacks allowed, according to Next Gen Stats, in a humbling 28-3 blowout.
Mims watched the tape. A decision was made. He was never going to play that poorly again.

Over a year later, Mims has more than lived up to his word. Through the first half of this season, Mims has developed into not only one of Cincinnati's best players but arguably the best right tackle in the NFL.
His performance, along with that of the rest of the offensive line, has helped turn the Bengals' passing attack into the best in the NFL.
Entering Monday's game against the Washington Commanders (8:15 p.m., ET, ESPN), Cincinnati leads the league in passing yards per game (298.9).
And as much as the team's big stars have contributed to that total, Mims also has been a big reason for that success.
"It's crazy how my game has evolved, man," he said this week. "It's been light-years different. I'm not nowhere near the same guy I was when I first came in this building."

The advanced metrics on Mims' play have been astounding. Per Next Gen Stats, Mims is second among all offensive tackles in one-on-one pass blocking rate. This season, he has been on an island on 87.6% of his total pass blocks. And yet, his pressure rate is the lowest among all tackles at 3.3%.
For the third-year player out of Georgia, the growth stems from one hard game in Denver.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The New York Yankees and right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga are in agreement on a two-year deal with a club option for 2029, sources told ESPN, reuniting the reliever and club after a season apart.
Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN.
Outfielder Gavin Sheets and the San Diego Padres are in agreement on a three-year, $11 million contract, sources tell ESPN.

The Colorado Rockies are acquiring right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Chicago White Sox, sources tell ESPN. The White Sox are getting LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz in return.
Right-hander Randy Dobnak and the Kansas City Royals are in agreement on a one-year, $1.35 million contract, a source tells ESPN.
Right-hander Sonny Gray and the Minnesota Twins are in agreement on a two-year, the team announced. The contract is for $55 million and includes an opt-out after the first season, sources tell ESPN.
